title: The Green Hornet
paragraphs: Modern urban masked-crimefighter adventure created at WXYZ.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: WXYZ local/regional era (January 31, 1936 to April 7, 1938) on [[org|org.a0d8a72797b5185f|WXYZ]], Mutual network era (April 12, 1938 to November 9, 1939) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Blue/ABC long network era (November 16, 1939 to September 8, 1950) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], and Final return (September 10, 1952 to December 5, 1952).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include George W. Trendle (creator, producer, and performer), Lee Allman (performer), Gilbert Shea (performer), Charles D. Livingstone (director), Rollon Parker (performer), Fran Striker (writer, performer, and editor), and Dan Beattie (writer and performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.a0d8a72797b5185f|WXYZ]], [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and [[org|org.666407112636e085|Michelson]].

The stories often return to extralegal crime fighting, organized crime and racketeering, espionage and sabotage, masked identity and disguise, newspaper journalism, and automobiles and the Black Beauty.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Interwar urban crime and racketeering culture, World War II sabotage and enemy-agent story shift, and Postwar network/station transition.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|the-lone-ranger|The Lone Ranger]], [[show|challenge-of-the-yukon|Challenge of the Yukon]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|boston-blackie|Boston Blackie]], and [[show|cbs-radio-mystery-theater|CBS Radio Mystery Theater]].
